nodes.label: Λ — a closed index of atomic transition cells
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A recoding of the quantum numbers rather than new physics, so whatever it exhibits is a property of indexing and not of atoms.

nodes.label: E(X) — the external definition cost
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Openness is a measurement, not a fault: E counts the cells a layout's own coordinates admit and the index denies, so it prices what must travel alongside an index.

nodes.label: ℛ — the reconstruction closure operator
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Defined from value sets and pairwise monotone bounds only, so ℛ(X) is exactly what a reader could rebuild from the cells alone with no outside knowledge.

nodes.label: Closed index — a fixed point of ℛ
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Closure gives six things and no others: alphabet, bounds, totality of the membership test, which cells may be added, which axes adjoined, which constraints imposed.

nodes.label: The periodic table is not a closed index
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the opening case because it is the most successful index in the physical sciences and its non-closure costs exactly thirty-six cells.

nodes.label: The thirty-six admitted-but-denied cells
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Twenty-five are forbidden by ℓ ≤ n−1 and eleven are deferred by the Madelung order; the decomposition was corrected once helium's slot was read as deferred rather than forbidden.

nodes.label: Helium's placement, and what E measures
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: E is a property of where helium is drawn, not of the elements: group 18 gives E = 36 and group 2 gives E = 20, so the choice costs sixteen cells to specify.

nodes.label: The transition cell (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Cells are transitions rather than states, which is why the title names an index of transitions.

nodes.label: The seven constraints, four origins
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Nothing enters Λ but Pauli, the hydrogenic radial solution, counting and angular-momentum coupling — the exhaustiveness is what lets the object's properties be attributed to indexing.

nodes.label: Every constraint is of the form xᵢ ≤ φ(xⱼ)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: No sum and no difference appears, because a set cut out by a sum bound is not closed.

nodes.label: The constraint graph is a tree — treewidth 1
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Three results follow from treewidth alone: the void needs no sieve, the order is recoverable by propagation, and the constraints offer no redundancy, so two-route defence must come from derived quantities.

nodes.label: The caps convention
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Counts are cap-dependent and the shape is not; the convention was in force from the first page and unwritten, so 69 of 84 cap-dependent paragraphs named no cap.

nodes.label: Λ is distributive
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The least surprising and most load-bearing fact in the chapter: it is what admits Birkhoff's representation.

nodes.label: Rank is conserved — modularity with equality
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Modular rather than submodular, and the equality is the signature of distributivity; the question came from celestial mechanics, which asks what an object conserves.

nodes.label: Modular rank is the cheaper test
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Pairwise O(n²) against triplewise O(n³), and a failure of modularity is a failure of distributivity, so it is found in half the work.

nodes.label: Seventeen join-irreducibles, twenty covers
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A fifty-seven-fold compression whose covers are the constraints made visible; the patterns hold across a range of caps, which licenses stating the poset once.

nodes.label: Sperner, and not rank-symmetric
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The rank sequence is log-concave hence unimodal, so Sperner holds rather than merely happening to; the skew measures how much more Pauli constrains than counting.

nodes.label: Particle–hole conjugation as a reflection of Λ
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Two competing self-duality counts were both right about their own reflection, and the discrepancy was definitional.

nodes.label: The arithmetic encoding — occupancy measure and Möbius function
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Two classical number-theoretic functions appear as lattice quantities, and the log of the occupancy measure is an ordinary ℓ¹ metric, which bridges additive and multiplicative slack.

nodes.label: The void
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Counted in closed form with no sieve, because a tree has no cycles for inclusion–exclusion to correct.

nodes.label: The single generating expression F
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One closed expression in six languages and a seventh in binary; F(1) = 976 and F(−1) = 2 have causes rather than being coincidences.

nodes.label: The one coupling, and it is the Pauli principle
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The expression's tree has exactly one coupling factor, which localises where the exclusion principle enters the generating function.

nodes.label: The Lach Cylinder — a cylinder over the transfer
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A cylinder and not a Möbius band; the shape is over ν rather than graded by ν, and the loop closes.

nodes.label: The cylinder is a fibration with two-body fibres
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: It does not factorise and then it does — a tower of fibrations terminating in boxes, which is what names the cylinder.

nodes.label: The tower — Λ₉ to Λ₁₃
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The ninth axis is what lets transitions compose; the coupling order is fixed as J_c, then K, then J.

nodes.label: The clock in the constraint — Λ₉'s composition has a direction
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The clock is an assumption and the assumption can be removed, which is why the arrows agree by a decay theorem rather than by fiat.

nodes.label: Self-reference — alphabet, order, bounds
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: S1 and S3 are cheap; S2, the order, is the hard one and works above d = 2 only by propagation along the tree.

nodes.label: Order recovery — Λ contains its own order
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Produced by refusing a conclusion: the author had concluded Λ did not contain its own order, and resuming from the refusal gave the theorem.

nodes.label: Self-defence — six defences, not three
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Closure never gives that the coordinates refer to anything, so three further mechanisms are needed and one of them cannot be run by the book at all.

nodes.label: The ⅅ_def / ⅅ_phys split
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A relation that cannot be violated by data is not empty — it defends the derivation rather than the data, and that single reframing produced the split.

nodes.label: Surplus — ⅅ ≥ 1 exactly when dim q > dim p
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Without surplus there is no check; for Λ the bound is tight at ⅅ = 2, and carrying more than it needs is the property the object was built to have.

nodes.label: The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The clearest evidence for the object: Z cancels from containment so the bracket held 56 of 56 and could not notice, while two quantities the method never uses were loud immediately.

nodes.label: The error class no structure catches
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A guard returned a null, a caller read it as false, and every relation downstream stayed consistent; what reached it was being asked to look again, which is why a collaborator is not optional.

nodes.label: Extension — E1 cells, E2 axes, E3 constraints
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: E is derived rather than postulated, so what may be added to a closed index is fixed by the closure rather than chosen.

nodes.label: An index carries what its coordinates carry, and no more
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The product structure is not what does the work, which is why ν is inadmissible as an axis and depth is not a coordinate function.

nodes.label: The law of realised closure
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Restated in certificate form because the first form had no falsifier: realised was never given a test, so the law was confirmed by naming and refutable only by failing to name.

nodes.label: E(X) is the prediction budget
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: An index may be complete or predictive and not both, because a prediction is a proposal about an unlisted cell and completeness is having none.

nodes.label: The negative results are the contribution
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Each strong negative came from defining a nothing rather than discarding it — perturbation bounds from a bracket's non-failure, impossibility from a search that found nothing.

nodes.label: Retrieval as a lattice problem
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A paywall blocks a source and not a cell, the secondary can beat the primary, and the retrieval graph is itself self-referencing.

nodes.label: ρ is a property of (document, route)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The chapter collapsed the second index; the route is a fibre, which §19.1 wrote without using it.

nodes.label: A language is a coordinate system
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Because the language a question is posed in bounds whether it can close, and a language can make a law monotone.

nodes.label: Translation, and E is the price
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One object and two namings: the certificate is a translation exhibited and checked, and there are exactly three ways a translation fails.

nodes.label: E = 0 is relative to coordinates
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The coordinates must be given with the claim, or a zero defect is unreadable.

nodes.label: The bracket — T(n) lies between T(n−1) and T(n+1)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: It fits nothing and assumes no functional form, returning an interval rather than a value: a fit says where a level probably is, the bracket says where it cannot fail to be.

nodes.label: The bracket's four rules
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Each rule is justified by ablation rather than by assertion, and Rule 1's second clause is not redundant.

nodes.label: The bracket is limit-free
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Limit-freedom has a computable price, which is what δ buys and what it costs.

nodes.label: A bracket whose admissible set is a singleton
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The same operation reads as a deduction about a quantity or as a uniqueness proof about a kind, and which it is depends only on how many admissible cells the interval contains.

nodes.label: The bracket's own boundary — inward deduction, outward not a bracket
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Inward it does not fail; past the last measurement it is not a bracket at all, and the falling widths show why.

nodes.label: The cost surface V = w/e = 4ν/3
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: V contains no σ, so no spectrometer can buy a narrower bracket: the price of certainty in a Rydberg series is set by the series.

nodes.label: The floor is algebraic before it is physical
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: V > 2 holds for any monotone sequence whatever, so every empirical V in the book is an instance of that bound and not an independent fact.

nodes.label: V is a function of ν/h alone
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Z and R cancel identically rather than approximately, which makes depth and step interchangeable.

nodes.label: The cost is the Newton decrement, and the term is self-concordant
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The quantity has a name in convex optimisation, which explains the cancellation and names an attribution the book owes.

nodes.label: The pole at p = 1
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: No guarantee exists for a linear observable, and the pole sits on the field's favourite variable.

nodes.label: The collection — 1,442 interior cells, 35 systems
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Spans ℓ = 0 to 6 and Z = 1 to 83 and the bracket holds in every cell; the census was computed rather than searched.

nodes.label: Four ways a species declines
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A structural exclusion covering five isoelectronic sequences came out of the four modes, which is three mechanisms rather than five exclusions.

nodes.label: A method that has never failed has not been tested
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The silence had to be made to carry a number before the result was falsifiable in the ordinary way.

nodes.label: The bound in the silence
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Reading the failure condition backwards turns every passing cell into an upper bound on local perturbation, obtained without fitting and without assuming smoothness.

nodes.label: The one deduction, and why it is not a prediction
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Offered as falsifiable rather than as a result, with an estimate inside a bracket because Rule 3 requires it and an earlier version violated it.

nodes.label: Collective sections and the assembly rule
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Collective coefficients are not a separate class; error amplifies as the exponent, which is the point rather than a defect.

nodes.label: Aitken's Δ² has an exact bias on a Rydberg series
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: And the bracket is the wrong tool there, which is a domain statement rather than a failure.

nodes.label: Slack — one quantity, three names
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: E(X), the void and V are all admitted against actual, differing only in whether the comparison is a difference or a ratio; the three languages agree because the three objects are one shape.

nodes.label: Slack is a description length
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Every structural result in the book is then a statement about slack.

nodes.label: The register — 1,171 withdrawn claims
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Not a confession but the material the method is made of: the errors were converted into structure, and each entry names which of four things caught it.

nodes.label: Where errors are caught
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Instrument-caught share rose from 5% to 25% while hand-caught fell from 88% to 55%, which is what a method becoming procedural looks like from inside.

nodes.label: Redundancy of paths, not redundancy of care
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The protocols were written and violated by the same person in the same week; what saved the results is that four different things were looking and not at the same thing.

nodes.label: The prime audits, ordered by what a failure costs
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: An audit that reads the wrong artefact will pass anything — 107 blank operator boxes across 44 pages passed every audit that read the source and not the page.

nodes.label: The principles P1–P23
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Three were corrected by the act of formalising them, and the twenty-three sort into mechanisms, operations and relations, which is what settles what each one owes.

nodes.label: The protocols
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The protocols are not advice; they are the failure modes of this work, inverted.

nodes.label: §2.14 — compute, then write
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Exists because writing conclusions before reading output was measured rather than deplored: it happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so no amount of care fixes it.

nodes.label: §2.20 — the prime directive, nothing runs unbounded
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Written after a computation was lost whole to a timeout.

nodes.label: §2.5 — census before search
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Prevents searching without targets; the protocol that should have stopped nine rederivations said enumerate before searching where it should have said search before deriving.

nodes.label: §2.19 — what a safe repair requires
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A repair can be riskier than the defect it fixes, so the register was examined before being repaired.

nodes.label: §2.17 — triangulation, three results locate a fourth
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: It is a check as well as a method, which is why it sits with the protocols.

nodes.label: §2.16 — the grid, the book's method stated
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Prevents hunting where a layout would show, and it classifies the whole of Q.

nodes.label: §2.18 — what is computable and what is decided
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Nothing tests a decision, so a decision checked as though computable is a fault the lattice itself can name.

nodes.label: The cypher analysis
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: It was not designed but noticed and then made explicit: ask each language in turn whether it can speak of an object, and read the kind off the pattern of silence.

nodes.label: The six languages and the question each asks
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: A language that falls silent is the finding, and the identity of the silent language names the kind of object.

nodes.label: An integer object — ordinal, algebraic, geometric, not analytic
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: It has no derivative and needs none, so fitting it is a category error.

nodes.label: The singleton criterion
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: ℛ cannot see it: an index is closed when its output class is a singleton, because two outputs mean the observer is still choosing and the choice is not in the object.

nodes.label: The domain protocol — never fit across a language boundary
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Enforced in code after every fit in a session had been applied to a whole quantity whose halves spoke different languages, so the constants kept absorbing one another.

nodes.label: The Löwdin challenge — derive the filling order
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The target is the ORDER, not n+ℓ: Madelung inverts 5d/4f and 6d/5f, so deriving n+ℓ exactly would mean deriving something false at two elements.

nodes.label: The occupation law ν(n,ℓ,q) = n − a√(n − ℓ − 1 + q/2(2ℓ+1))
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Both Pauli quantities appear, the radicand is the count of states below, and occupancy enters only through Pauli, so the law needs no new coordinate.

nodes.label: The corridor — L(Z) < a < U(Z)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One linear inequality per rival, all 106 intervals non-empty, nineteen distinct surds, and no measurement enters.

nodes.label: The walk — `a` carried and reset eighteen times
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The state is necessary: with no carried value 104 of 106 steps admit several self-consistent subshells, so the periodic table is not computable from a single atom's configuration.

nodes.label: The entry point t(ℓ) → √(ℓ(ℓ+1)/2)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Fixed by a single-state observation, the ionisation energy, and ℓ(ℓ+1) is the centrifugal term — the only place ℓ enters the radial equation.

nodes.label: Λ_var — the variables of the problem on (body, role)
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: No coordinate relates the Rydberg electron to the nucleus directly, which is the screening statement appearing as a fact about the coordinates rather than about the interaction.

nodes.label: The three ladders, and the isotopic fourth
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Only two of three electronic quantities are independent, so no ladder varies Z alone and the isotopic ladder is the only route to the nucleus.

nodes.label: f is outside the domain and the law says so
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: At an f opening the node count hits its floor and L = −∞, so the missing test is forbidden by structure rather than by missing data.

nodes.label: One object, six appearances, six disciplines' names
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: ℓ(ℓ+1) had been recorded as gate, collapse switch, barrier, Seaton's ratio, angular factor and entry point before the microscope collapsed them.

nodes.label: The reorderability law
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: One statement read in two regimes: arity ≤ 3 is bijunctive and linear, arity ≥ 4 contains 1-in-3-SAT and no Schaefer class covers it.

nodes.label: The step law
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Growth from minimal reorderable sets reaches every reorderable set, and the largest reorderable proper subset of the full box is three quarters with a subcube removed.

nodes.label: The interval machinery, and what it actually was
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: C1P, monotone endpoints and PQ-trees are a representation of a 2-colouring; the reason d = 2 is easy is that two cells in two dimensions differ on at most two axes.

nodes.label: Precedent, and what a search can bound
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Novelty is not the author's to claim, so what is claimed instead is the bound a search establishes; nine results were rederived from scratch that were already in print.

nodes.label: Q — the open questions, indexed and closed
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The grid applied to the book's own open items, with each item's closing cost stated; P7's well-founded measure was already computed there.

nodes.label: The law applied to this book
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: The book is an index and is made to satisfy its own method, with the recursion shown safe because the logic has no negation.

nodes.label: Which of the book's figures survive their own inputs moving
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: An identity survives a changed input and a value does not, which is why a value without its cap setting is a reading whose conditions are missing.

nodes.label: The method outside spectroscopy
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Celestial mechanics gives families rather than trajectories, the nucleus a second index of the same construction, and string theory three objects on the pole.

nodes.label: The Calabi–Yau catalogue, indexed
nodes.author: Matthew Lach
nodes.rationale: Self-duality measured, the thin tip read as a defect of the construction, and E(X) on a specifiable slice giving 540 predictions.
